item.title: Mammary glands of domesticated livestock and humans could harbor avian influenza
item.description: An ongoing outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza has affected more than 184 million domestic poultry since 2022 and, since making the leap to dairy cattle in spring 2024, more than 1,000 milking cow herds.

item.title: Nanoflower-treated stem cells deliver healthier mitochondria to stressed cells
item.description: This study shows that vacancy-engineered MoS₂ nanoflowers drive mitochondrial biogenesis in human mesenchymal stem cells by activating SIRT1–PGC-1α signaling and reducing oxidative stress. These treated cells transfer more functional mitochondria to injured recipient cells, restoring energy metabolism and redox balance in multiple in vitro models.

item.title: SwRI and Trinity researchers work on next-generation intranasal therapy for PTSD
item.description: Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) and Trinity University are developing an intranasal (IN) drug-device combination to treat post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

item.title: Blinking suppression reveals how the brain filters speech in noisy environments
item.description: Blinking is a human reflex most often performed without thinking, like breathing. Although research on blinking is usually related to vision, a new Concordia study examines how blinking is connected to cognitive function such as filtering out background noise to focus on what someone is trying to say to us in a crowded room.

item.title: State-funded multidisciplinary model improves care for adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
item.description: Adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) often lose access to specialized care once they age out of pediatric services.

item.title: New arts and wellbeing program supports the social needs of families affected by dementia
item.description: A new arts and wellbeing program co-developed by the University of South Australia, Flinders University and the University of Adelaide shows that supporting the social needs of people living with dementia and their carers can help families rediscover connection, confidence and a sense of community.

item.title: SIRT3 deficiency worsens eustachian tube dysfunction during middle-ear infection
item.description: Middle-ear infections caused by Gram-negative bacteria remain among the most common pediatric illnesses worldwide.

item.title: Researchers discover new biomarker of "complicated" mild- to severe-pediatric traumatic brain injury
item.description: Researchers at the University of Pittsburgh and UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh discovered a promising new biomarker of "complicated" mild- to severe-pediatric traumatic brain injury, or TBI.

item.title: Sterilized fermented beverage targets obesity and type 2 diabetes pathways in computational study
item.description: Researchers profiled a terminally sterilized probiotic-fermented MFH beverage and identified aporphine alkaloids and flavonoids with favorable predicted ADMET properties. Integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and 100-ns MD simulations suggest multi-target engagement of metabolic-inflammatory pathways relevant to obesity and type 2 diabetes.

item.title: National study maps where food additives come from in children’s and adults’ diets
item.description: By analysing nationally representative diet data, researchers show that food additives rarely occur alone, with children and teenagers experiencing the highest exposure to complex additive mixtures largely driven by ultra-processed foods.
